title: Genius Might Be Simpler Than You Think
html:
Good morning,

Josh Billings said: “Genius ain’t anything more than elegant common sense.”

How true is that?

Some of the best ideas seem ridiculously obvious once someone else has thought of them.

You look at them and say, “Why didn’t I think of that?”

That’s the genius.

Not making something more complicated to prove how clever you are.

Making the difficult easy.

Making the complicated simple.

Looking at something everyone else accepts and thinking, “There must be a better way to do this.”

Simple ideas can be difficult to find because we get used to the way things are.

We follow the same process.

Put up with the same frustration.

Explain the same confusing thing again and again.

Eventually, we stop noticing that it could be easier.

But common sense asks useful questions:
* Why do we do it this way?
* Does this step need to be here?
* Could someone understand this without an explanation?
* What would make this easier for the next person?

The answers may improve a system at work, remove an unnecessary job at home, or make life easier for someone you care about.

That matters, because unnecessary complexity doesn’t just waste time; it uses energy and attention that could be spent on better work, important goals, or the people around you.

You don’t need a revolutionary invention to bring out your genius. You might simply find a clearer way to explain something.

Remove a step that serves no purpose. Put something where people naturally look for it.

Solve a small irritation everyone else has learned to tolerate. And when you do, someone may look at your solution and say:

“Why didn’t I think of that?”

Exactly!

This Week’s Monday Motivator

Genius doesn’t always mean creating something extraordinary.

Sometimes it means noticing what is unnecessarily difficult and having the common sense to make it simpler.

Prompt for the Week

What is one thing I do regularly that is more complicated than it needs to be?

How could I make it simpler, easier or better this week?

To your success!

Glenn
